correctness.rationale: For each nonconstant affine word, choose its least active digit and partition into blocks containing one Q-zero subblock. Adjacent zero subblocks can merge only once, giving only Q/2Q runs and the exact zero-window formula. A highest-nonzero-coefficient cyclic block translation proves constant-term invariance. A carry-by-carry count yields M=1_{H_{s-1}=1}+(p-1) sum_{t=0}^{s-2} p^{s-t-2}1_{H_t=1}. The prefix-sum coefficient transformation is invertible, giving the exact polynomial F_s and multiplicity p(p-1). The proof handles j=m-1, b=1 and b>2Q and is supplemented by 117 independently calculated complete enumerator comparisons.

value.rationale: The question is motivated by the coordinate-order-sensitive overlapping-read b-symbol metric on the classical first-order Reed–Muller family. The theorem calculates the entire weight spectrum and codeword multiplicities for every odd prime, every dimension, and every cyclic window length. Its digit-carry structure and sparse polynomial with 2^s distinct admissible join counts are nontrivial finite-field combinatorics, not an arbitrary isolated example, a mere minimum-distance corollary, or a relabeling of the known binary case.
